source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check Mini DP can work with resolution change
1.Power on SUT and boot into OS.
2.Change the current video resolution and color depth to low
3.Choose the "Test" button to test the changes, then choose "Apply" to accept the changes.
4.Shutdown and restart the OS, then login.
5.Review Event Viewer logs to confirm there are no errors or fault conditions reported.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1.All selectable changes up to 800X600 at a 16 bit color depth should function properly. Higher resolutions may not work properly because of limitations of the video driver used and the supported resolutions of the monitor used.
2.Screen can display w/o error.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Resolution change down: change the video resolution/color depth down (e.g. to 1024x768@16bit) in the OS display settings. Requires a person at the Mini-DP display + OS desktop GUI to click Test/Apply; agent can read the current mode via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "xrandr 2>&1 | head -20; readlink /sys/class/drm/card*-* 2>&1" if a GUI session is present, but the GUI resolution change is operator/visual.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the current xrandr/DRM resolution list so the user confirms the resolution change-down to 16bit applied correctly on the Mini-DP display; the GUI change + visual check are operator.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: resolution change is a GUI/visual check on the Mini-DP display - operator performs it; agent only reads the OS mode.

original_test_intent: Verify the approved lower-resolution MiniDP mode set, explicitly including the source's 800x600 at 16-bit criterion, displays without error and remains usable through restart/login with clean logs.
original_method: An engineer selects the owner-confirmed low-mode matrix in the OS GUI, uses Test and Apply, visually checks the physical display, restarts/logs in and reviews Event Viewer and supporting logs.
manual_activity: The source requires GUI Test/Apply plus human confirmation that the low-resolution image remains visible and correct before and after restart. Those are core acceptance activities.
required_inputs: Owner clarification whether 800x600 is the target/minimum and which selectable lower modes are included
OS build, GPU/driver, MiniDP path and monitor/EDID
16-bit colour semantics and visual acceptance criteria
Maintenance approval, prior mode, physical operator and alternate console
safety_requirements: Do not substitute DeepSeek's unstated 1024x768 example for the 800x600 source criterion.
Do not apply an unadvertised low timing/depth or assume the output mapping.
Keep a known-good revert mode and independent KVM/console before restart.
Stop on blank/corrupt/scaled-unusably image, driver fault or failed login; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect OS-native EDID, supported/active mode, depth and event data for each approved low mode.
Track the exact owner-confirmed matrix and restart state.
Compare logs/readback while leaving visual usability and PASS/FAIL to the engineer.
engineer_actions: Resolve the low/800x600 matrix and approve recovery.
Perform GUI Test/Apply, visually inspect each required low mode and restart/login.
Issue the formal verdict from full evidence.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not suitable as written. It introduces 1024x768 without source authority, assumes Linux despite Event Viewer, and its read-only output cannot prove GUI application, 16-bit colour, visual quality or restart persistence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use OS-native documented read-only display and event inventory after the owner resolves the target matrix; preserve 800x600 explicitly.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Low-mode change, source 800x600/16-bit criterion, GUI Test/Apply, restart/login, Event Viewer and 10/5-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: TARGET MATRIX CLARIFICATION REQUIRED; RETAIN HUMAN VISUAL CORE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record the approved lower-mode set with 800x600 explicitly addressed, capture electronic mode/depth after each GUI application, photograph a diagnostic pattern for scaling/legibility, restart at the selected final mode and export display events.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact OS, GPU/driver, MiniDP path and monitor.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS build, GPU driver/firmware and EDID.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner interpretation plus OS/GPU/monitor supported-mode documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an explicit matrix and rejects the invented 1024x768 example without altering source coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No 800x600 requirement is dropped; additional modes are only those owner-approved.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Low modes may be scaled by the display; electronic mode readback cannot prove legibility or artifacts.

project_override_considerations: The project must state its exact lower-mode matrix and may choose a final restored mode. A smaller matrix is only project-plan completion. Missing clarification is execution readiness, not a permanent BLOCKED case.
expected_evidence: Owner-approved low-mode matrix explicitly addressing 800x600 and 16-bit
Per-mode GUI, electronic and visual evidence plus successful restart/login
Event Viewer/system/BMC/SEL review, restoration and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: 'Low' and 'up to 800x600' are imprecise but not irreconcilable; the owner can define the exact matrix without altering the test's low-resolution intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target clarification is needed for execution, but the core method and 800x600 anchor are clear enough to retain a non-blocked library classification.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject the invented 1024x768 target and xrandr-only coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its target-clarification, display-stack and recovery requirements while applying MANUAL ONLY to the GUI/visual core.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Treats ambiguity as readiness, preserves the literal 800x600 fact and keeps evidence/verdict roles separate.

review_improvement: Prevents an unauthorized 1024x768 substitution and defines evidence for scaling/legibility at the actual low-mode target.
independent_technical_reasoning: The exact low matrix needs owner input, but that does not erase the source's human GUI and physical-display acceptance. The core remains MANUAL ONLY and is not permanently blocked.
